## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

All ten discourses possess direct Chinese parallels in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicle 21, discourses SĀ 567–575) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus aligns the text closely with T 99 as well as Sanskrit and Tibetan doctrinal treatises, including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records substantial textual reuse with the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), various books of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya*, and the two *vedalla* discourses of the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 43 and MN 44), which closely match the catechetical interrogations found in SN 41.6 and SN 41.7 [DharmaNexus; Nyanaponika et al. 2003].
